claims.title: Exact product observation channel and prefix Blackwell monotonicity
claims.scope: a finite rational observation channel repeated conditionally independently for a fixed hidden source-law scenario
assumptions: the hidden scenario remains fixed across repetitions
signals are conditionally independent and use the same declared channel
the longer history is deterministically projected to a retained prefix
nonclaims: conditional independence is a model assumption rather than a universal sensor law
Blackwell dominance need not produce strict value improvement for one declared loss

claims.title: Signed count is sufficient for symmetric binary repeated evidence
claims.scope: two fixed hidden scenarios and a binary symmetric observation channel with accuracy in [1/2,1)
assumptions: scenario zero and scenario one interchange the two signal probabilities
nonclaims: ordered history can matter for nonsymmetric or stateful observation channels
terminal likelihood sufficiency does not by itself include an installed-action state under switching costs

claims.title: Fair-tie symmetric majority has exact even-sample plateaus
claims.scope: binary symmetric repeated observations with majority decision and a fair public tie break
assumptions: ties at an even sample count receive one-half decision credit
nonclaims: an even observation is not Blackwell-equivalent to the preceding odd history
the plateau is loss- and symmetry-specific rather than a generic no-value-of-data theorem

claims.title: Exact bounded sequential public-signal policy-tree coding game
claims.scope: finite rational source-law scenarios, a fixed public rational observation channel, finite horizon, deterministic zero-error prefix codebooks, and rational switching cost
assumptions: one hidden source-law scenario remains fixed throughout the horizon
the period codebook is a deterministic function of the complete public signal prefix
policy, code, dominance, no-signal sequence, and game support enumerations complete below configured caps
nonclaims: the policy does not observe the hidden scenario or true source law
full policy-tree enumeration is not a scalable large-horizon algorithm

claims.title: Exact sorted Pareto frontier for two-scenario policy costs
claims.scope: distinct exact rational two-scenario cost vectors produced after complete bounded policy-tree enumeration
assumptions: cost pairs are sorted by increasing first coordinate and then increasing second coordinate
componentwise dominance is the pruning relation
all raw policies complete below the declared policy cap
nonclaims: the O(N log N) frontier step does not remove exponential complete policy-tree enumeration
three or more source scenarios require a different multidimensional frontier method

claims.title: Two-scenario K3 repeated observations have exact terminal and sequential values
claims.scope: complete K3, heavy-state scenarios (4/5,1/10,1/10) and (1/10,4/5,1/10), and a binary symmetric observation channel of accuracy 3/4
assumptions: public signal histories and optional source-independent shared policy randomness
the sequential example has horizon three
nonclaims: the exact fractions are specific to the declared finite instance
additivity of prefix decision values is not asserted for arbitrary minimax scenario families

claims.title: Bounded exact repeated-observation and policy-tree audit
claims.scope: the product channels, history projections, binary evidence classes, policy trees, switching expectations, and exact games exercised by repository tests
assumptions: all configured history, policy, dominance, code, sequence, and game support caps complete without truncation
Python Fraction arithmetic is used for finite channel and cost calculations
nonclaims: CI success is not a continuous-observation or scalability theorem
finite coding-game values are not evidence that reality is simulated
